title: The Zero Train: × 10, 100, 1,000 … 1,000,000
description: All aboard! Find out why multiplying by 10, 100, 1,000 and more just adds zeros to the end of a number.
intro: Your number is a train, with one car for each digit. 48 is an engine pulling a 4 car and an 8 car.
Numbers like 1,000 are trains too: a 1 car pulling three 0 cars. To work out 48 × 1,000, unhook the three 0 cars and couple them onto the back of the 48 train. Now it says 48,000!
The 1 car gets left behind, and that's fine: multiplying by 1 doesn't change anything.
Once you've got the trick, the helper train goes away. Count the zeros, take that many 0 cars from the depot, and press Go!
